description: The CAN Dataset Generator publishes the CrySyS team's code for producing vehicle-network anomaly-detection scenarios from CAN traffic traces. The repository accompanies the fabrication and masquerade benchmark and includes a sample CAN trace for testing the workflow. Its documented entry point is a Python script requiring Python 3.10 or later. Outputs are organised by trace identifier and include a jobs.json record of executed generation jobs. GitHub and the README explicitly state GPL-3.0, permitting free reuse of the source code. The generator has no intrinsic geographic coverage or calendar period; these follow its input traces and chosen scenarios. It can prepare controlled disturbance cases for evaluating detection models in vehicle digital twins and network-resilience studies, alongside general network tools such as platform-ns-3. A caveat is that trace generation does not itself establish how a physical vehicle or controller will respond. Users must distinguish offline transformations from any hardware-dependent test procedure. This review read metadata and documentation without executing the generator or interacting with a CAN network.
